verdict: HP grew revenue 13% to a record third-quarter $15.7 billion — selling fewer PCs (units down 16%) but much pricier ones — and raised its full-year outlook, though a tariff refund flattered the profit line.

segments.name: Personal Systems
segments.note: PCs and workstations — commercial revenue rose 22% and consumer 10%, even though total unit shipments fell 16%: buyers chose pricier, premium and AI PCs.

segments.name: Printing
segments.note: Printers and supplies. Printing revenue was $3,912M before a $2M other/eliminations line; supplies fell 3% while printing margins stayed rich at 18.1%.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Designing PCs, printers and the WXP work platform.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Sales, marketing and running the company.

opex.name: Amortization of intangible assets
opex.note: Writing down the value of acquired brands and technology over time.

otherDetail: Interest and other costs, net — $94M taken out of profit.

takeaways.title: Fewer PCs, more money
takeaways.text: Personal Systems shipped 16% fewer units but took in 18% more revenue — memory-supply improvements let HP fulfill premium orders, and buyers are choosing AI PCs and workstations over cheap machines.

takeaways.title: Tariff refunds helped
takeaways.text: GAAP EPS of $0.71 includes an $0.11 benefit from tariff refunds. Even without it, non-GAAP EPS rose 11% to $0.83, and HP raised its full-year EPS and free-cash-flow outlook.

takeaways.title: Printing still prints money
takeaways.text: Printing revenue slipped 2% to $3.9 billion, but at an 18.1% operating margin it earns roughly four times the margin rate of PCs (4.6%) — the quiet profit anchor of the company.

oneTimers: GAAP EPS includes an $0.11-per-share favorable impact from tariff refunds; HP's non-GAAP EPS of $0.83 includes it too.
The year-ago quarter contained one-time tax and litigation benefits, which is why GAAP EPS looks down 11% year over year even though non-GAAP EPS rose 11%.
Restructuring and other charges were $48M in the quarter.
